text:
Talia Benson: beta retro thread for incident-bot v2. drop quick bullets: what worked, what was noisy, what needs to change before GA. pls be specific (cards, links, thresholds, permissions). :memo:

Rafael Mendes: overall: huge win vs v1. “first 5 min” felt way less ad-hoc. but we have some sharp edges.

Miles Thornton: +1. biggest time saver was Recent Deploys card. we stopped spending 10 mins asking “did anything ship?”

Aisha Bello: from the SLO side, error budget burn links were used a lot. people clicked those immediately instead of hunting dashboards.

Jacob Stein: Saturation card helped in the partial region outage test (gpu util + queue depth + admission). BUT it gets noisy fast when it dumps too many lines.

Devon Price: can we list by card?

Devon Price: Recent Deploys: A+
- surfaced service + image sha + rollout phase
- canary status + link to PR was clutch
- suggestion: show “deploy started X min ago” (relative time) so you don’t do mental math

Connor O’Brien (via Devon Price): also: sometimes “no deploys found” was wrong b/c service mapping missing. we need the canonical service registry lookup in the join.

Miles Thornton: yep, the join issues caused confusion twice. responders assumed “not deploy related” when it was.

Ethan Park: for join: we can fall back from `service_id` -> `k8s_app` label -> service registry. should be in the deploy metadata exporter not the bot.

Priya Natarajan: +1 push it upstream. bot should not have N mapping hacks.

Logan Wright: Saturation card:
- what worked: summarizing “GPU util p95 / queue depth / KV cache pressure” in one place
- what didn’t: pulling per-pool + per-model breakdowns by default. too much + query cost.
- proposal: default = 3 numbers + a single deep link to “Saturation Overview” dashboard w/ time window. expand-on-click for details.

Allison Grant: +100. on-call wants “is this saturation-ish?” not 20-series. also the KV pressure label names were confusing (kv_cache_evictions vs kv_cache_pressure). can we standardize copy?

Jacob Stein: also the thresholds. right now GPU util > 85% turns yellow, > 95% red. but for some pools 90% is normal.

Aisha Bello: we should use queue depth + backpressure as the “red” signal, not raw GPU %. GPU stays high during healthy batching.

Ravi Menon: agree. if admission control is shedding or scheduler backpressure engaged, that’s actionable red. GPU alone is context.

Miles Thornton: +1. in one beta incident, GPU util scared folks but queue was flat and latency was fine.

Dylan Brooks: ok so: re-rank signals by actionability:
1) backpressure/admission engaged
2) queue depth trend / queued_ms
3) KV evictions/pressure
4) GPU util
and make GPU util not scream unless paired w/ queue.

Devon Price: Config Diff card:
- most helpful when it showed: feature flag flips + routing policy changes + quota changes
- biggest issue: “diff too big” and then responders just give up
- ask: smart truncation: show top N changes + “view full diff” in modal

Mina Haddad: routing policy diffs were the #1 win for my team. we had at least one “503 after config push” where it would’ve saved ~20 mins.

Kevin Osei: + reminder: the redaction warnings were good. but we need the audit event to include “diff viewed in modal” vs “summary rendered in thread”. compliance asked.

Devon Price: ack. modal view is a separate interaction so easy to log.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (via Kevin Osei): permissions: some responders got empty Config Diff card due to missing scope. we need a clearer message than “not authorized”. include who to page + break-glass steps.

Rafael Mendes: yes pls. the empty card is worse than no card. it reads like “no changes”.

incident-bot: (beta stats) context completeness (last 14 days, beta cohort)
- Deploy context present: 83%
- Config diff present: 61%
- Saturation summary present: 78%
- Error budget links present: 92%
Top failure reasons:
- config diff auth denied (19)
- telemetry query timeout (11)
- service mapping missing for deploy join (7)

Logan Wright: telemetry query timeouts: we still see tail lat spikes when multiple incident threads start clicking “expand”. caching helps but we need request coalescing across threads.

Dylan Brooks: coalescing is in progress (ENG-5427). we also need stricter budgets: if query > 2s, return cached + link + “try again”.

Allison Grant: degraded mode behavior was pretty solid when it actually triggered. but the messaging could be clearer:
- “Live telemetry unavailable; showing last-known-good from X min ago”
- include a single link to the dashboard w/ same params

Aisha Bello: +1, and mark stale data in the card header so it’s obvious.

Chloe Martin: deep links: people liked them, but a few links landed on wrong region/time window.
- time window should anchor to incident start (or thread_ts) by default, not “last 1h now”
- also: preserve service + route filters even when tenant is omitted (tenant-safe)

Marissa Cole: product POV: wins:
- “copy command” snippets in cards got used (kubectl/log query)
- responders asked for one more action: “open in Console > Rollouts” from deploy card
- noise: too much text in thread; push details to modal

Miles Thornton: +1. thread readability matters. during sev1 i want a clean summary i can paste into the incident doc.

Rafael Mendes: suggestion: add a “Copy incident summary” button that composes a short block:
- suspected trigger (deploy/config/unknown)
- top signals (saturation/backpressure)
- key links

Devon Price: feasible. we can generate a markdown-ish snippet.

Priya Natarajan: any other papercuts?

Jacob Stein: config diff semantics: sometimes a staged rollout shows diff but it’s only 10% of fleet. we should display propagation status (region / %).

Ethan Park: that requires config service to expose rollout phase (or last-applied vs effective). we can at least show “change is still propagating” if not converged.

Mina Haddad: + for routing changes: show “policy effective in regions: us-east, us-west; pending: eu-west”.

Kevin Osei: make sure we don’t leak tenant identifiers when we list “effective scopes”. keep it to region/pool/service.

Talia Benson: summarizing action items I’m hearing (pls react :thumbsup: if accurate):
1) Recent Deploys: add relative time; fix service mapping/join upstream; ensure “no deploys found” is confidence-labeled
2) Saturation: default to minimal + actionable ordering; reduce breakdowns; adjust thresholds (less GPU-centric); standardize KV/backpressure naming
3) Config Diff: smart truncation + modal pagination; better empty-state messaging; add propagation/rollout phase when possible
4) Telemetry: enforce query budgets; improve caching + coalescing; clearer degraded-mode copy + stale indicator
5) Deep links: anchor to incident start/thread_ts; fix region/time params; add Rollouts link
6) Security: audit modal views distinctly; improve break-glass guidance

Miles Thornton: :thumbsup:

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: also: we need a checklist before GA: runbook updates + “what to do if card missing”

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: + alert tuning alignment: if bot highlights backpressure, alerts should match so people trust it.

Logan Wright: :thumbsup: i’ll own the “minimal default saturation + expand” behavior w/ Dylan/Devon.

Devon Price: :thumbsup: i’ll own truncation + modal pagination improvements.

Kevin Osei: :thumbsup: i’ll follow up with exact audit event fields compliance wants.

Marissa Cole: :thumbsup: for GA, please keep the thread output short. we can ship detail in Console.

Talia Benson: cool. I’ll turn these into a GA readiness list + owners. keep adding notes if you remember more.
